newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee posts heavy losses as supply woes ease.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee posts heavy losses as supply woes ease.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices plunged to their lowest settlement in three weeks on Monday, as commodity funds sold heavily amid an easing of short-term supply concerns, market sources said.

With future prices nearly doubling since early December, traders said more coffee has found its way to exchange warehouses as producers took advantage of the highest prices in nearly two-and-a-half years.
In the past two weeks alone, CSCE certified stockpiles have nearly tripled to 47,233 60-kg bags after a rise of 2,250 bags as of Friday.
"Things are not as bullish as they were two weeks ago," Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "Stocks are increasing and prices are going down."
"I think the party is over," he added.

The most-active May contract suffered the heaviest losses, plummeting 17.70 cents -- or more than nine percent -- on the day, to 168.65 cents a lb, after ranging from 185.90 to 167.65. Spot March, which expires on Tuesday, slid 7.35 cents, to 197.65 cents. The rest fell 11.75 to 15.20 cents.
Some traders said an anticipated increase in Green Coffee Association (GCA) stockpiles may have also calmed supply worries.

After Monday's close, GCA data showed that supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose by 204,000 60-kg bags in February to 1,546,000 bags -- their highest level in five months. Most dealers expected the February data to show a rise of up to 100,000 60-kg.

By comparison, U.S. green coffee stocks rose by a modest 15,000 bags last month. Stockpiles in February of 1996, however, were still some 50 percent higher than current levels, at 2,221,000 bags, up 70,000 bags from the previous month, GCA said.
Despite the recent build up in stockpiles, traders said future prices should continue to be well underpinned by low inventory levels.
"I think you could see prices drop to 160-150," one trader said. "But they will probably bounce back up. The situation is still very tight"
Technically, traders said downward momentum accelerated late in the session after the active May contract fell through key support levels at 179.00, then 175.00, triggering a series of sell-stops.
They said May delivery should find good support near 160.00, while 175.00 would provide near-term chart resistance.
Turnover was estimated at 18,352 lots, compared with Friday's official tally of 12,130 lots. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk +1 212 859 1640))
